A wug test of German noun plurals

Source: R/data.R
german_plurals.Rd

60 adult native speakers of German give the plural of 48 nonce nouns, each presented with its article (der, die, das). The plural ending depends on gender and on how the noun ends: schwa-final and feminine nouns mostly take -(e)n, nouns in -el/-er mostly no ending, masculine and neuter nouns ending in a consonant mostly -e, and nouns ending in a full vowel -s. Speakers differ in how readily they use -s. A five-way outcome.

Usage

german_plurals

Format

A tibble with 2880 rows and 7 columns:

participant

Participant ID, P01 to P60.

item

Item ID, i01 to i48.

nonce

The nonce noun, e.g. "Pünde".

article

"der", "die" or "das".

gender

"masculine", "feminine" or "neuter".

final

How the noun ends: "schwa", "-el/-er", "consonant" or "full vowel".

plural

"-e", "-(e)n", "-er", "-s" or "zero".

Source

data-raw/german_plurals.R

Details

True model: each gender-by-ending cell has its own probabilities for the five endings (see data-raw/german_plurals.R), perturbed on the log scale by a by-participant preference for -s (SD 0.6) and by response-level noise (SD 0.3).

References

Berko, J. (1958). The child's learning of English morphology. Word, 14(2-3), 150-177. doi:10.1080/00437956.1958.11659661

Examples

table(german_plurals$final, german_plurals$plural)
#>             
#>               -e -(e)n -er  -s zero
#>   schwa       41   525  16  63   75
#>   -el/-er     49   219   8  84  360
#>   consonant  277   234  79  94   36
#>   full vowel  22    82  19 555   42
